svg.title: E-commerce on Azure: availability zone failure
svg.text: What shoppers and on-call actually see
Built in advance, or it does not work
Scenario: zone 2 of East US 2 goes dark at 20:14 on a Friday
Every zonal and zone-redundant service handles it differently. This is what each one does, and what you have to have built beforehand.
In-flight requests on zone 2 pods fail. Front
Door shows a burst of 502s and 504s.
Load balancer probes and kube-proxy stop
sending to zone 2. Redis and Search promote
Azure SQL completes its zone failover. Apps
with retry logic reconnect on their own.
HPA sees CPU climb on the remaining pods and
autoscaler adds nodes in zones 1 and 3, if
Pods stuck on unreachable nodes are finally
Nothing rebalances by itself. Roll the
• Each zone sized to carry 50% of peak, not 33%
• topologySpreadConstraints on zone, PDB per service
• One node pool per zone, or NAP with zone spread
• ZRS disks for anything stateful left in AKS
• Retries with backoff on SQL, Redis, Search clients
• Idempotent checkout so a retried POST is safe
• Alert on Front Door 5xx by origin, not CPU
• Chaos Studio zone-down drill every quarter
